venue.name: Legacy Downtown Art Gallery (UVic)
venue.description: Legacy Downtown is the street level gallery of the University of Victoria Legacy Art Galleries, the university's art museum, at 630 Yates Street in downtown Victoria. It shows changing exhibitions drawn from and alongside UVic's collection of over 18,000 Canadian, Indigenous and international historic and contemporary artworks. Free exhibition introductions are offered to university classes, school classes and community groups of all ages, booked by email. The gallery is open Wednesday to Saturday, 10 am to 4 pm.

facility_notes.washrooms: Legacy has two single-stall, gender inclusive washrooms. Both of these washrooms have manual doors and only one provides ample space for mobility devices. The larger bathroom is equipped with a baby changing station.
facility_notes.wheelchair_accessible: The main entrance to Legacy is at street level and there are no steps or gaps to enter the main gallery, inner gallery or washrooms. The main entrance has two sets of heavy doors with push buttons. The classroom space and private offices are located on the second floor of Legacy. These can only be accessed by a flight of stairs.

venue.hours_notes: Wednesday to Saturday, 10 am to 4 pm. Closed Sunday, Monday and Tuesday.
venue.seasonal_notes: Legacy Downtown is currently closed for installation and reopens September 16 with two new exhibitions. It is also closed Wednesday September 30 for the National Day for Truth and Reconciliation.

programs.name: Group visit with exhibition introduction
programs.description: A group visit to the current exhibitions with a short introduction from gallery staff. Offered free to university classes, school classes and community groups of all ages. To book, email the gallery with your group name, how many people are coming, which exhibitions you would like to see, your preferred date and time, and any special needs your group has.
programs.what_children_do: Walk through the gallery rooms with a short spoken introduction to the exhibitions, then look at and talk about the works on the walls.
programs.our_note: The gallery is a small street level space, so this is a short visit rather than a morning out. There is nowhere on site to eat that the gallery mentions, so plan lunch somewhere else. Ask which of their two galleries you are booked into, downtown or on campus, because the booking address is the same for both.
programs.practical_summary: Free, step free from the street, with two single stall washrooms and a baby change table in the larger one. Lunch space, bus parking, group size limits and how much notice they need are not published, so ask when you email.
programs.evidence: We offer free exhibition introductions for university classes, school classes, and community groups of all ages.

gaps: Admission price for the downtown gallery is not stated anywhere on the site. Only the campus gallery is listed as free, so ask whether walking in costs anything.
No age or grade range is published for group visits. The tours page says groups of all ages, which is the only guidance given.
Group size limits are not published, so a large class may need splitting.
How much notice they need for a booking is not stated.
How many adults have to come is not stated.
How long a group visit lasts is not stated.
Nothing is said about somewhere to eat lunch, indoors or out.
Nothing is said about where a bus can drop off or park. The site mentions metered street parking and the Bastion Square parkade about two blocks away.

The two Legacy galleries, downtown and on campus, share one website, one phone number and one booking email, and the tours page does not say which gallery a group visit happens in. This record covers the downtown gallery at 630 Yates Street only. Worth confirming the location when you book.
Workshops are listed on the site but are described as currently on hold, so no workshop was recorded.
The site's map embed gives only a map viewport rather than a published pin, so coordinates were left for geocoding from the street address.
The Open Graph image on the home page is a black line illustration rather than a photograph, so the exterior photo from the visit page was used as the main image instead.
